question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping’s continued dominance of the Chinese Communist Party, reinforced by sweeping purges across the Politburo and Central Military Commission, underpins the overwhelming trader consensus that he will remain in office through the 21st Party Congress in 2027. Recent leadership gatherings, including the Beidaihe conclave, and the absence of any designated successor or visible elite opposition signal institutional consolidation and a focus on loyalty ahead of his anticipated fourth term. Ongoing anti-corruption campaigns have removed senior figures without disrupting core decision-making structures. While near-certain pricing reflects this stability, health developments, an acute economic shock prompting elite realignment, or an unprecedented postponement of the congress could still introduce uncertainty before the end of 2026.

question: Will Gavin Newsom win the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the named individual wins and accepts the 2028 nomination of the Democratic Party for U.S. president. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

Any replacement of the democratic nominee before election day will not change the resolution of the market.

eventMetadata.context_description: The 2028 Democratic presidential nomination market remains tightly clustered because the field is wide open more than two years out, with no candidate yet consolidating broad party support after the 2024 cycle. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Gavin Newsom, and Jon Ossoff lead on national visibility, executive records, and Senate positioning, respectively, while recent DNC calendar changes—placing South Carolina first on January 22, 2028, followed by Nevada, New Hampshire, New Mexico, Michigan, and Virginia—shift early emphasis toward diverse voter blocs. Upcoming 2026 midterms, early fundraising, and positioning on economic and border issues represent the next catalysts that could create separation in an otherwise fragmented contest.
